title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-07

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard captures a loose ’70s free‑form set with standout Cumberland Blues, Sugar Magnolia and The Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording offers crystal‑clear soundboard fidelity that even preserves an onstage anti‑war protest spoken during Drums.  Musically the show is a happy‑hour of free‑form acoustic‑electric jamming – fans repeatedly point to the blazing Cumberland Blues, the debut Sugar Magnolia and a powerful stretch of The Other One as highlights.  Minor complaints focus on track‑splitting quirks rather than the performance itself.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (9 out of 11) are 4–5 stars and praise both the audio clarity and the musical moments; only a few note track‑splitting issues, so overall rating is strong.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with great instrument separation; anti‑war speech captured intact. Some reviewers complain about the way tracks are split (e.g., The Other One broken into multiple files) but this does not affect overall sound fidelity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Described as a free‑form ’70s show with acoustic and semi‑electric sections, loose transitions, political spoken interludes, and an unstructured, jam‑heavy second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for great tone and playing throughout the set (e.g., “Jerry played at set between the Dead's acoustic and electric sets”).
band_member_comments.Bob: Mentioned in a friendly sign‑off (“Peace, Bob”) but no specific performance comment.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums segment noted for strong playing and the captured anti‑war protest speech.
